subject.title: Support multiple gateway tokens for multi-user session isolation

question: Should OpenClaw add a native Gateway multi-token principal model for Control UI/WebChat token-mode users, and should it be unified with the scoped-token work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/92367?
rationale: The request changes public auth config, credential matching, caller identity, session isolation, authorization semantics, and security posture, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent boundary.

options.title: Unify Gateway Principals
options.body: Define one Gateway-owned principal model covering per-user token identity, scoped service tokens, SecretRefs, rotation, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To User Labels
options.body: Implement only token-to-user labels and session identity for Control UI/WebChat now, accepting a likely later migration into the scoped-token model.

options.title: Keep External Front Layers
options.body: Decline native multi-token auth for now and document trusted-proxy or Pinchy-style front layers as the supported team-deployment path.

recommendation.title: Unify Gateway Principals
recommendation.body: Define one Gateway-owned principal model covering per-user token identity, scoped service tokens, SecretRefs, rotation, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current identity-bearing trusted-proxy Gateway auth path this decision would extend or deliberately keep separate.
